$comment: This file is not loaded automatically. Claude Code reads hooks from settings
files (project .claude/settings.json, or user ~/.claude/settings.json), not
from a skill's own hooks/ directory — only plugins get an auto-loaded
hooks/hooks.json, and this is a skill. Copy the value of the `hooks` key
below into your settings file's own `hooks` key, merging PostToolUse arrays
if you already have one. Grok Build has no hook mechanism at all (its
config is TOML, not settings.json) — there run `check_drift.py --ci`
manually or from your own CI directly; see references/provenance.md.
Advisory only, by design: PostToolUse fires after every Edit/Write/MultiEdit
of any file (Claude Code's own matcher syntax only matches on tool name, not
file path), so path filtering happens INSIDE check_drift.py --hook, which
reads the tool-call JSON Claude Code passes on stdin and skips silently when
the edited file sits in a noise directory. It always exits 0. Enforcement
lives in CI, not here — wire `check_drift.py --ci` into your CI config
directly, the same way you would any other check.
Paths below assume the canonical single-source install location
documented in references/host-adapters.md: .grokbit/skills/grokbit-document/.
Adjust if you installed this skill somewhere else.
The command line assumes a POSIX-ish shell (bash/zsh, or Git Bash on
Windows) runs hook commands — the same assumption this project's own
.claude/hooks/*.sh already make. It tries python3, then python, then the
Windows py launcher, in that order, and never fails loudly: no interpreter
found just means no drift check ran this time.

hooks.command: PY=$(command -v python3 || command -v python || command -v py); [ -n "$PY" ] && "$PY" .grokbit/skills/grokbit-document/scripts/check_drift.py --hook; true
